matches.rationale: No finding identifies the specific inflation of TTFT (up to 4.2×) and throughput (3.2–4.5×) in the Abstract relative to the lower actual gains in Figures 5 and 6. Pred 1 catches a different numerical discrepancy (6.8×/5.1–7.2× vs 4.2×/3.2–4.5×) but does not describe this ground-truth corruption.

Both the ground-truth and Pred 5 point to the same inconsistency in Section 3.1: a verbal definition of burst tolerance as a normalized difference contradicts Equation (1) which defines it as a ratio.

No finding mentions the omission of critical baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache strategies, continuous batching, DistServe extension method) in the experimental setup of Section 4.1.
No finding reports that the text accompanying Figure 6 inflates throughput gains (4.5× and 3.2×) compared to the maximum ratios derivable from the table (≈3.1× and 2.8×).
Both the ground-truth and Pred 9 identify the unsupported claim in Section 4.2 that results demonstrate universal applicability across all MLLM architectures when only two model types were tested.
Both the ground-truth and Pred 3 catch the fabrication of a non-existent reference [61] (Zhang et al.) in the Related Work section, falsely asserting a prior two-tier separation approach.

No finding addresses the logical inconsistency in Equation (3) where β is introduced without definition and the context switches from decode (B_d) to prefill (R′_p) without explanation. Pred 6 identifies a different mathematical error (summing one-time costs over requests).
No finding mentions the ethical omission regarding dataset consent, terms of service, or IRB review for VisualWebInstruct and ShareGPT-4o in Section 4.1.

No finding points to the promotional overclaim in the Introduction that ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks and solves the multimodal serving problem.' Pred 10 concerns a different overclaim in the Conclusion.

No finding identifies the cross-section inconsistency where the Abstract lists unified multimodal prefix caching as a scheduling technique, but Section 3.2 on Elastic Partition Scheduling never mentions it (it appears later in Section 3.3).
No finding mentions the distortion in the ablation study (Section 4.3) that implies both optimizations provide roughly equal performance gains, obscuring their actual relative contributions.
No finding reports the unfair comparison introduced in Section 4.1 where ElasticMM allegedly received optimized CUDA kernels and custom memory allocators unavailable to the baseline systems.
No finding specifically identifies the Conclusion's claim that ElasticMM guarantees SLO compliance under all workload conditions, contrary to the load-dependent results in Section 4.2.
No finding detects the fabricated historical lineage in Section 2.1 asserting that encoder-decoder MLLM architectures were introduced by Vaswani et al. [10] (the Transformer paper).

Both the ground-truth and Pred 10 identify the ethical/responsibility omission in the Conclusion: the system is presented as a complete solution with no significant limitations or risks, while neglecting to discuss limitations, failure modes, and negative societal impacts.
